newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-CREEVEY PUTS QUEENSLAND BACK IN FRONT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CREEVEY PUTS QUEENSLAND BACK IN FRONT.

text.p: Pace bowler Brendan Creevey took five wickets on Thursday to hand Queensland an unexpected advantage on the second day of their Sheffield Shield match against Victoria.

Queensland's batsmen had earlier struggled to reach 229 in their first innnings, with Victoria looking to press home their advantage with a solid reply on the second day of the match at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
Creevey put paid to those plans by tearing through the Victoria top order as the hosts succumbed for 191 just before the close.
Creevey finished with five for 32 from 20.3 overs, after taking three of the first four wickets to fall as Victoria slumped to 73 for four.
Number four Rohan Larkin offered the only significant resistance of the Victoria innings with 52.
Queensland had earlier resumed on their overnight score of 218 for eight, with all-rounder and medium-pacer Ian Harvey taking the last wicket to finish with five for 45.
